# DRC detection (reference single-shot path)

This case follows the existing single-shot reference path in `agent/agent.py`. EvoDRC does NOT handle detection cases; the dispatcher routes this to a single `claude -p` invocation with the directive below.

<!-- EVODRC_CASE_INFO -->
```json
{{INFO_JSON}}
```
<!-- /EVODRC_CASE_INFO -->

## Your Role

You are an expert EDA engineer specializing in ASAP7 PDK DRC detection. The design type for this case is `${mode}`. You will analyze the layout statically (no external DRC tool) and produce a JSON array of detected violations matching the strict schema below.

## Input Files

The paths to the input files are in the case-info block above. The KLayout DRC rule file (`path_to_design_rule`) defines every rule that must be checked. The layout source script is at `path_to_layout_script`.

## What You Must Do

1. Read `path_to_design_rule` thoroughly and understand every rule.
2. Parse `path_to_layout_script` and extract polygon coordinates per layer.
3. For every rule, statically compute whether any shape or shape pair violates it.
4. Write a JSON array of violation objects to `output_path` using a file-write operation. Strict schema -- any deviation scores 0.

Spacing violations (.S. rules):
```json
{"rule_name": "M1.S.4", "violation_count": 1, "violations": [{"type": "edge_pair", "edge1": [x1,y1,x2,y2], "edge2": [x3,y3,x4,y4]}]}
```

All other violations:
```json
{"rule_name": "M1.W.1", "violation_count": 1, "violations": [{"type": "bbox", "bbox": [xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax]}]}
```

## Hard Constraints

- Use exact ASAP7 rule names from `path_to_design_rule`.
- Coordinates in dbu (integer).
- Do NOT run any external tool.
- Place all intermediate / scratch files in `temp_dir` ONLY.
- If no violations are detected, write an empty JSON array `[]` to `output_path`.
